title: Tenant noise drift isolation scratchpad - Sasha Patel
content:
Context:
Quick personal notes and running log for tests exploring multi-tenant interference / latency drift over long runs. The goal is to validate that our serving runtime can maintain tail SLOs under low-level noisy neighbors and to identify easy isolation knobs (cgroups, CUDA MPS tweaks, CPU pinning, mem limits).

Summary (top-line):
- Repro: Stable p50 but p95/p99 drift upward after ~30m in mixed-workload tenant.
- Hypothesis: NVMe burst GC + occasional host CPU steal from other containers + periodic model compaction kicks.
- Immediate mitigations that looked promising in short runs: disable host-level cron tasks on test node, enforce CPU shares for worker containers, limit IO bandwidth for background tenants.

Environment:
- Cluster: perf-edge-04 (shared testbed), 8x NVIDIA A100 (80GB).
- Runtime build: inference-runtime v0.37.1+local (kernel tweaks: cudnn 8.2, CUDA 11.8).
- Models used: rwin-13b-fp16 (baseline), rwin-13b-q4_0 (quantized).
- Serving config: dynamic-batch=true, max_batch_size=8, kv_cache=true, async_prefetch=on.
- Client: redwood-bench v0.12 (custom), traffic generator: synthetic conversational traces (mix of short/long requests).

Test matrix (high level):
1) Single-tenant baseline (dedicated GPU) — run 2h, concurrency=16, report per-minute p50/p90/p95/p99 + qps
2) Two-tenant noisy (main workload + background mem-intensive tenant) — background runs at 0.6 GPU util, main same as baseline
3) Multi-noise: background tenants x3 (IO heavy, short-burst CPU, long-tail low qps)
4) Isolation knobs: CPU pinning, cgroups cpuset, MPS disabled/enabled, nvme throttling (fio), container io.weight

Commands used (bench):
- baseline: ./redwood-bench --host perf-edge-04:443 --model rwin-13b-fp16 --concurrency 16 --duration 7200 --rate-limit 0
- background fio: sudo fio --name=bgwrite --filename=/dev/nvme0n1 --size=10G --bs=1M --iodepth=32 --rw=write --runtime=3600
- collect perf: sudo sar -n DEV 60, iostat -x 60, nvidia-smi dmon -s u, ps aux --sort=-%mem | head

Raw snapshot (selected excerpts, minute-resolution aggregate):
- Single-tenant (2h window) 
  avg_qps: 650, p50=12ms, p90=28ms, p95=45ms, p99=110ms, errors=0.05%
- Two-tenant noisy (first 30m)
  avg_qps: 640, p50=13ms, p90=32ms, p95=60ms, p99=180ms, errors=0.2%
- Two-tenant noisy (30-90m)
  avg_qps: 620, p50=15ms, p90=48ms, p95=120ms, p99=420ms, errors=0.9%
- Multi-noise (three backgrounds, 90m window)
  avg_qps: 590, p50=16ms, p90=55ms, p95=200ms, p99=950ms, errors=3.1%

Ascii p99 drift (per-minute snapshots, short form):
(0m) 110 | (10m) 130 | (20m) 140 | (30m) 180 | (40m) 250 | (50m) 320 | (60m) 410 | (70m) 370 | (80m) 360 | (90m) 950
Note: big jump at 90m correlates with NVMe GC event on host (dmesg shows garbage-collect/trim logged at +89m).

Observations / possible signals correlated with p99 spikes:
- NVMe background write pressure correlated with long tails — observed device_util spiking to 98% and queue avg wait rising.
- CPU steal: at times the host showed ~20% steal on a few cores — aligns with periodic cron backup on a different container.
- GPU context switching (MPS disabled) reduced tail variance slightly (p99 lowered ~15%), but throughput marginally impacted (-4% qps).
- KV cache churn: when long context (>2048 tokens) requests appear, KV eviction increased CPU scheduling and briefly blocks serving threads -> tail blips.

Experiment: isolate NVMe with fio throttling (limit-bg):
- fio cgroup with blkio.weight lowered for tenants -> p99 improved from 420ms -> 160ms in 30-90m window. Errors dropped to 0.3%.
- downside: background tenants suffered throughput, acceptable for internal multi-tenant SLA tests.

Intervention: CPU pinning & cpuset for serving container
- Pin main serving threads to isolated cores (no other containers scheduled) -> p99 drops ~20% across all noisy scenarios, throughput stable or slightly up.
- Implementation: systemd slice + cpuset.cpus set to dedicated range, kernel isolated= on boot for test nodes.

Quick checklist of actionable mitigations to try cluster-wide:
- Enforce blkio weights or throttling for non-critical tenants on shared test clusters
- Use CPU isolation slices for latency-sensitive serving containers by default (systemd unit templates)
- Consider enabling MPS for high-concurrency stable workloads, but gate by noise-cases (feature flag)
- Add nvme GC awareness to autoscaler / admission control (reject background IO-heavy jobs on serving nodes)

Unresolved questions / next experiments:
- Is the NVMe GC frequency predictable? Run longer test (48h) with periodic snapshots and fio simulation of steady-state write pattern to trigger GC deterministically.
- Quantify cost of isolation knobs on overall cluster utilization (how much capacity lost if we reserve N cores per serving container).
- Evaluate H100 nodes: do they show the same drift pattern? (likely not NVMe bound but CPU steal still matters)

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Run longer 48h baseline on h100-perf-02 with identical workload and no background tenants; record per-minute device stats. (ticket: ENG-4830)
- Draft a lightweight operator to set blkio for non-critical pods via admission webhook (sketch in PR#2345).
- Share this scratchpad with SRE and Capacity planning; schedule a run on staging with more realistic customer traces (not synthetic).

References / quick links:
- dmesg excerpts: /var/log/dmesg.2025-01-14.gz (see trim/gc events around +1h30)
- perf dashboard: https://perf.redwood.internal/dash/tenant-noise/2025-01-14
- related ticket: ENG-4821 (background job scheduling causing CPU steal)

End notes: This is a working scratchpad — experiments are rough, lots of noise in the testbed. Main takeaway: hardware-level IO events and host CPU scheduling are first-order contributors to tail drift in mixed-tenant scenarios. Proper IO and CPU isolation prevents most of the observed p99 spikes without complex changes to the inference runtime.
